subject: Co-sell & Azure Private Offer: packaging and marketplace artifacts
messages:
From: Nina Roy <nina@clearscale.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearScale Marketplace Team <marketplace@clearscale.com>
Date: 2028-01-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood + ClearScale co-sell listing — initial packaging 

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the call this morning. ClearScale is ready to move forward with an Azure Private Offer for the joint solution (managed deployment + Redwood inference credits). Before we spin up the offer, a few asks from our side so we can line up our GTM and procurement teams: 

- Confirm recommended "offer shape" (SaaS managed offer vs VM image + ARM template).
- Any SKU naming conventions you prefer for co-sell attribution and metering signals?
- A checklist of required marketplace artifacts (ARM template, one-click deployment link, logo sizes, technical evidence).
- Draft mutual action plan (MAP) and contact for co-sell enablement from Redwood (for sales engineering and partnership ops).

We attached a short one-pager about our deployment options; happy to fill gaps. Could you loop in whoever will own the artifacts on Redwood's side?

Appreciate it — aiming for Private Offer submission by end of January so our procurement cycle can align.

Best,
Nina
Partnerships Manager | ClearScale
Attachment: clearscale-deploy-options.pdf (PDF, 86 KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Nina Roy <nina@clearscale.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-09T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood + ClearScale co-sell listing — initial packaging

Thanks, Nina — great to kick this off. Looping in Olga (partner ops), Karthik (platform integrations), and Ben (field leads) to get the artifacts and MAP aligned. A couple quick answers and next steps from our side: 

- Offer shape: we recommend a Managed Offer (SaaS) for co-sell clarity. It gives the cleanest metering and is preferred by Azure co-sell teams. If ClearScale needs a VM-based option for isolated networks we can support a secondary VM offer, but prioritize Managed Offer for the co-sell.

- SKU naming: use the pattern RW-CLRS-<tier>-<unit> (e.g., RW-CLRS-PRO-HR). We'll provide a canonical SKU file.

- Required artifacts (short): ARM template (if VM option), managed-offer manifest, SaaS fulfillment URL, product icons (48/128/512), security evidence summary (SOC2 excerpt + data flow diagram), and an internal sales one-pager.

Action items: 
1) Olga, can you assemble the marketplace checklist and the intake form we submit to Azure?
2) Karthik, can you confirm the minimum API contract and sample ARM snippet we should include for the VM pathway?
3) Ben, can you share the co-sell contact spreadsheet and draft MAP language for discounts/commission?

Nina — I attached a first-pass MAP and an Offer spec spreadsheet (placeholders) to accelerate. Olga will coordinate evidence pickup with your marketplace team.

Cheers,
Hannah
Director, Alliances | Redwood Inference
Attachments: rwin-MAP-draft-v1.pdf, azure-offer-specs.xlsx

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina Roy <nina@clearscale.com>
Date: 2028-01-10T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood + ClearScale co-sell listing — initial packaging

On Mon, Jan 9, 2028 at 11:03 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Nina — great to kick this off. Looping in Olga (partner ops), Karthik (platform integrations), and Ben (field leads) to get the artifacts and MAP aligned. A couple quick answers and next steps from our side: 

Thanks Hannah — I put together a checklist and timeline below (high level) for ClearScale so they can prepare artifacts. Nina, copying the items we typically need for Azure co-sell intake: 

Marketplace intake checklist (what we need from ClearScale):
- Offer manifest (for Managed Offer): service description, fulfillment endpoint, SLA language
- SaaS fulfillment URL and ping endpoints for provisioning
- Billing/metering spec (unit definitions, aggregation window)
- Security evidence: SOC2 summary, data retention policy, encryption at rest/in-transit statement
- Logos + marketing copy (one-pager)
- Technical evidence: sample ARM template or container deployment manifest (if they choose VM path)
- Contact for Microsoft co-sell (partner ID) and ClearScale procurement contact

Timeline suggestion: 
- Jan 10–13: ClearScale provides artifacts and completed intake spreadsheet
- Jan 16–19: Redwood packaging + internal compliance review
- Jan 20–24: Partner joint review and final edits
- Jan 25–27: Private Offer submission to Azure (target)

Notes/risks: 
- If ClearScale's procurement requires a VM image for air-gapped customers, that will add ~2 weeks (image validation).
- We should confirm whether ClearScale wants Redwood credits or a blended managed-service SKU; that affects SKU definitions.

I'll open a shared Drive folder and add the checklist and template files. For now I've attached the intake template and our standard evidence checklist. Nina — can you confirm the partner ID and whether procurement wants invoices routed through ClearScale or Redwood?

Thanks,
Olga
Partner Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: marketplace-intake-template.xlsx, evidence-checklist.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina Roy <nina@clearscale.com>
Date: 2028-01-11T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood + ClearScale co-sell listing — initial packaging

Olga — thanks for the checklist and timeline. A couple technical clarifications from the platform side: 

- For Managed Offer we only need a SaaS fulfillment URL that accepts our provisioning token; we'll provide the token exchange spec. The minimal contract includes create/delete/provision webhook endpoints.
- SKU metering: prefer usage-by-token with hourly aggregation for credit consumption. If ClearScale needs seat-based SKUs we can map those to a conversion rate but that reduces co-sell visibility.
- ARM/VM path: provide a parameterized ARM snippet (resource group, VM size, storage account). We can sign off on a test image but require a compatibility matrix for GPU drivers.

I'll draft a short API spec and an ARM snippet and upload to the Drive folder Olga creates. Ben — once we have the MAP finalized we should capture the lead-assignment rules for co-sell crediting (MDM: who registers the Azure opportunity).

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Integrations | Redwood Inference

> On Jan 10, 2028, at 08:27, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Nina — can you confirm the partner ID and whether procurement wants invoices routed through ClearScale or Redwood?
